introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geography 3 (0750), Paper 3, ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2021. Duration: three and a quarter hours.**

Answer FOUR questions in all. Answer question ONE and three others, choosing ONE question from SECTION B and TWO from SECTION C. Question ONE carries thirty-one marks and the rest carry twenty-three marks each.

Only the required number of questions will be marked.

In answering questions on this paper, you are encouraged to refer to your own field and practical work where relevant. Credit will be awarded for such references.

Candidates are advised NOT to attempt the questions on field investigations if such an exercise has not been carried out.

Marks will be awarded for well annotated maps and diagrams where these are relevant.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Calculators are allowed.

Materials required: Topographic maps, Graph Paper and two outline maps of Cameroon.

Le sujet imprimé ne répète pas l'en-tête « SECTION B » devant la question 3 : elle est rangée en Section B parce qu'elle suit la question 2 (Field Work and Techniques) et que la Section C (Cameroon) ne commence qu'à la question 4.
Carte : le sujet prévoit un fond de carte du Cameroun fourni le jour de l'épreuve (non reproduit dans le PDF) ; le corrigé décrit le coloriage et la légende sans figure.

« Western Industrial Triangle » : l'expression n'est pas définie par le sujet ; les limites exactes diffèrent selon les manuels, le corrigé retient Douala, Edea, Limbe et l'Ouest et le dit. Les noms d'usines (ALUCAM, SONARA, etc.) et les matières premières sont des repères reconnus cités de mémoire, sans chiffres ; à vérifier par un spécialiste avant mise en avant.
Les points des sous-questions (7 + 10 + 6) font bien 23 marks.

questions.enonce_markdown:
5. a) Using the outline map of Cameroon provided, locate and briefly describe the main vegetation types in Cameroon. **(7 marks)**

*[outline map of Cameroon supplied on the day, not reproduced here]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Method.** On the outline map, shade or hatch each vegetation zone, add a key, a title (*Vegetation zones of Cameroon*) and the names of main towns for reference; then describe each zone in the text. The zones follow the **decrease in rainfall from south to north**, modified by relief.

| Vegetation type | Location | Characteristics |
|---|---|---|
| **Equatorial (tropical) rainforest** | South, South-East, East and the coastal parts of the South-West and Littoral | Evergreen trees of 30 to 40 m or more, in several layers, dense canopy, climbers and epiphytes, little undergrowth, trees such as mahogany, iroko and ebony; heavy rainfall throughout the year |
| **Mangrove forest** | Coastal creeks and estuaries (Wouri estuary, Rio del Rey, Ndian, Campo) | Stilt-rooted trees of salt-tolerant species (red mangrove), muddy and saline swamps |
| **Montane vegetation** | Mt Cameroon, Bamenda Highlands, Mt Oku and the Adamawa and western ranges | Altitude zones: montane forest, then tall grassland and bamboo, and lower temperatures on the summits |
| **Guinea (woodland) savanna** | Adamawa Plateau and the central parts of the country, and the Western grassland lowlands | Tall grass 2 to 3 m high mixed with scattered deciduous trees; fire-resistant trees; long wet season |
| **Sudan savanna** | The Benue lowlands and the north (Garoua area) | Shorter grass with scattered trees such as acacia and baobab, deciduous trees which shed leaves in the dry season |
| **Sahel (thorn) savanna** | The Far North (Mandara foothills, Lake Chad plains) | Short, tufted grass and thorny scrub (acacia), a few baobabs, very low and irregular rainfall |

(Shading and key: 2 marks; correct location of at least four types: 2 marks; descriptions: 3 marks.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
b) i) Identify major industries and their sources of raw materials in the Western Industrial Triangle. **(10 marks)**

ii) What efforts have been put in place to boost the industrial sector of Cameroon? **(6 marks)**
questions.corrige_markdown:
### (i) Industries and raw materials (10 marks)

**The area.** The Western Industrial Triangle is the industrial area of the south-west and littoral part of the country, centred on **Douala** (with Bonaberi), and including **Edea**, **Limbe** and the towns of the west, such as **Nkongsamba and Bafoussam**; its exact boundaries vary between textbooks. Its advantages are the **port of Douala**, hydroelectric power from the Sanaga (Edea and Song Loulou), railways and roads, a large market and labour force.

| Industry | Examples / places | Sources of raw materials |
|---|---|---|
| **Aluminium smelting** | Edea (ALUCAM) | Alumina imported by sea; electricity from the Sanaga hydroelectric stations |
| **Brewing and soft drinks** | Douala, Bafoussam, Limbe | Barley malt (partly imported), sugar, maize, sorghum and water from local sources |
| **Cement** | Douala (Bonaberi) | Clinker/limestone largely imported, with local sand and aggregate |
| **Oil refining** | Limbe (SONARA) | Crude oil from the offshore fields of the Rio del Rey/Gulf of Guinea basin and imported crude |
| **Agro-processing** (palm oil, soap, rubber, banana packing) | Douala, Edea, Dibombari, Limbe | Oil palm, rubber and bananas from the nearby plantations of the Littoral and the South-West |
| **Timber processing** | Douala, Edea | Logs from the forests of the South and East, brought by rail and road |
| **Textiles** | Douala | Cotton from the North, plus imported fibres and dyes |
| **Metal and engineering works, shipbuilding and repair** | Douala | Imported steel and spare parts |

(1 mark for each industry correctly identified with its raw materials, maximum 10 marks.)

### (ii) Efforts to boost the industrial sector (6 marks)

- **Investment incentives:** an **Investment Code** and the Investment Charter give tax and customs relief to investors; the **industrial free zone** regime for export-oriented firms.
- **Infrastructure:** extension of electricity (new dams such as **Lom Pangar** and **Memve'ele** and gas-fired plants), the **deep-sea port of Kribi** and the improvement of the roads and the railway.
- **Privatisation and reform** of State-owned companies since the 1990s, and the creation of **industrial zones** (for example around Douala and Bonaberi).
- **Support for small and medium enterprises** through training, credit, upgrading programmes and one-stop services for business creation.
- **National development strategies**, such as the Growth and Employment Strategy Paper and **Vision 2035**, which aim to make Cameroon an industrialised emerging country, and **regional integration** (CEMAC) to widen the market.
- **Promotion of local transformation of raw materials** (cocoa, coffee, timber and cotton) to add value before export.

Any six well-explained efforts earn full marks.
